title: On Missing the coach by five minutes
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：miss　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 miss 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 the director ① missed the coach by five minutes in silence, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the director ② misses the coach by five minutes twice over without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ miss the coach by five minutes at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ missed the coach by five minutes before — a line in the poster for August 1956 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Missing the coach by five minutes in silence, the director said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ miss the old house for years twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Miss the old house for years at once and never mention it again.

By 1969 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the poster, and a new actor from the next theatre ⑧ misses the old house for years in silence every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stage, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ missed the coach by five minutes again when nobody else would.

⑩ To miss the coach by five minutes, my mother said in 1974, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the theatre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the theatre forgets, somebody misses the coach by five minutes twice over again and somebody must miss the coach by five minutes in silence all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 错过（一般过去式 missed the coach by five minutes：1962 年导演头一回这样做，一言不发地）
B. v. 错过（一般现在 misses the coach by five minutes：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 错过（不定式 to miss the coach by five minutes：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 错过（过去完成时 had missed the coach by five minutes：1956 年八月的戏报上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 错过（动名词 missing the coach by five minutes 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 想念（miss the old house for years：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去想念多年都惦着那座老屋）
G. v. 想念（miss the old house for years：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 错过（后段两处：新来的演员照例 misses the old house for years，而母亲又一次 missed the coach by five minutes）

answers.why: miss 意为“错过”，1962 年导演一言不发地错过差五分钟没赶上那班车，那是戏院里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 missed。
miss 意为“错过”，自那以后导演来回两遍把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 misses。
miss 意为“错过”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯错过差五分钟没赶上那班车”，此处为不定式 to miss the coach by five minutes。
miss 意为“错过”，戏报里 八月 那行字说明早在 1969 年之前就有人错过过，故用过去完成时 had missed。
miss 意为“错过”，导演说“错过差五分钟没赶上那班车这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 missing the coach by five minutes 作主语。
miss 意为“想念”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去想念多年都惦着那座老屋”，should ever 之后用原形 miss the old house for years。
miss 意为“想念”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻想念多年都惦着那座老屋（miss the old house for years at once），以后再也不要提起。
miss 意为“错过”，新来的演员每个夜晚都照例想念多年都惦着那座老屋，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 misses。
miss 意为“错过”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次一言不发地错过差五分钟没赶上那班车，用一般过去式 missed 叙述。
miss 意为“错过”，结尾那句是母亲 1974 年的话：要错过差五分钟没赶上那班车，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和戏院记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 miss 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1962 the director missed the coach by five minutes in silence, and nobody in the theatre forgot it.
Even now the director misses the coach by five minutes twice over whenever the theatre asks.
Missing the coach by five minutes in silence, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever miss the old house for years twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new actor from the next theatre misses the old house for years in silence every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother missed the coach by five minutes again, and the theatre remembered that half.
